title: Electromagnetic fields act via activation of voltage-gated calcium channels to produce beneficial or adverse effects
finding: VGCC activation is the primary mechanism of non-thermal EMF bioeffects. 23 calcium channel blocker studies confirm: blocking VGCCs blocks EMF effects.

title: Wi-Fi is an important threat to human health
finding: 28 studies show calcium channel blockers prevent EMF effects. VGCC voltage sensor has 7.2 million times higher sensitivity than thermal prediction.

title: Proton dynamics in voltage-gated calcium channel selectivity filter
finding: Grotthuss proton hopping in VGCC selectivity filter provides quantum-level mechanism for EMF sensitivity at non-thermal intensities.

title: Nerve cell damage in mammalian brain after exposure to microwaves from GSM mobile phones
finding: BBB permeability increased at SAR 0.016 W/kg — 100x below safety limits. Neuronal damage in cortex, hippocampus, basal ganglia.

title: Oxidative mechanisms of biological activity of low-intensity radiofrequency radiation
finding: 93 of 100 peer-reviewed studies reported oxidative stress increases at sub-thermal RF levels. Confirms VGCC/Ca2+/ROS pathway.

title: Umbrella review of EMF biological effects
finding: 39 systematic reviews confirm biological effects of non-thermal EMF exposure across multiple endpoints.

title: Resonance effects indicate a radical-pair mechanism for avian magnetic compass
finding: RF at Larmor frequency disrupts magnetic compass in birds. Confirms radical pair mechanism. Disruption threshold ~15 nT.

title: Anthropogenic electromagnetic noise disrupts magnetic compass orientation in migratory birds
finding: Man-made electromagnetic noise in 2 kHz-5 MHz band disrupts compass orientation. Shielding restores it. First demonstration of anthropogenic EMF ecological impact.

title: The radical pair mechanism of magnetoreception
finding: RPM is the leading hypothesis for magnetoreception. Cryptochrome radical pairs sensitive to Earth-strength magnetic fields.

title: Low-intensity EMF activates CRY-dependent circadian pathway in Drosophila
finding: Pulsed EMF activates CRY-dependent signaling at non-thermal intensities in Drosophila. CRY is the transducer.

title: Cryptochrome mediates light-dependent magnetosensitivity in Drosophila
finding: CRY mutants do not respond to magnetic fields. Wild-type does. Confirms CRY as magnetoreception transducer.

title: FAD-superoxide radical pair mechanism in cryptochrome
finding: CRY FAD-superoxide radical pair responds to Earth-strength fields via asymmetric recombination.

title: Non-monotonic magnetic field effects in planarians confirm RPM predictions
finding: RPM non-monotonic predictions confirmed in planarian worms. Biological compass effects measurable in simple organisms.

title: EMF effects on pineal melatonin production
finding: EMF exposure suppresses pineal melatonin production. Melatonin regulates GnRH pulsatility.

title: Light at night, chronodisruption, melatonin suppression, and cancer risk
finding: Melatonin suppression -> GnRH disruption -> HPG axis dysregulation -> reproductive consequences.

title: EMF exposure and corticosterone elevation in rodents
finding: EMF exposure elevated corticosterone with large effect size d=1.88. Confirms chronic HPA axis activation.

title: EMF exposure and depression risk
finding: EMF exposure associated with depression OR 1.45. HPA-mediated mood dysregulation.

title: Mobile phone use and salivary cortisol
finding: Mobile phone use >2h/day associated with elevated salivary cortisol. N=200.

title: A population-level decline in serum testosterone levels in American men
finding: Age-independent T decline 1.2%/yr 1987-2004. Persists after BMI/smoking/health control.

title: Meta-analysis: secular testosterone decline 1971-2024
finding: Linear negative regression across decades in >1M subjects. Confirms Travison.

title: Decline in serum testosterone in adolescents and young adults
finding: T decline particularly severe in younger males. Suggests environmental cause.

title: Meta-analysis: EMF effects on testosterone (29 animal studies)
finding: EMF -> T down, SMD 0.87 (95% CI 0.43-1.30), mean SAR 0.9 W/kg.

title: Testosterone is associated with mating success but not attractiveness or masculinity in human males
finding: T correlates with mating success via courtship effort, not physical attractiveness. T makes men more active approachers, not more attractive.

title: Exogenous testosterone influences sexual overperception bias
finding: Exogenous T increases tendency to interpret women's signals as sexual interest. T down -> reduced overperception -> fewer approaches. RCT.

title: Testosterone causes both prosocial and antisocial status-enhancing behaviors in human males
finding: Exogenous T causally increases status-seeking behavior. Not just aggression but strategic social behavior. RCT confirms causal direction.

title: The dual-hormone hypothesis for social status
finding: T effects on status behavior manifest ONLY when cortisol is low. High cortisol blocks T behavioral expression. EMF raises cortisol AND lowers T -> double lock.

title: Meta-analysis of dual-hormone hypothesis (30 studies, N=8538)
finding: T x cortisol interaction significant for status-relevant behavior (r=-.061, p=.026).

title: Human fluctuating asymmetry and sexual behavior
finding: Women attracted to T-produced traits (masculinity, symmetry) as signals of genetic quality.

title: The polyvagal theory: phylogenetic substrates of a social nervous system
finding: Myelinated vagus inhibits HPA and enables social engagement. Chronic stress -> vagal suppression -> OT down -> social bonding down.

title: Oxytocin and vasopressin in the evolution of sociality
finding: OT/AVP fundamental neuropeptides enabling mammalian sociality, pair bonding, and parental behavior.

title: Oxytocin and social affiliation in humans
finding: OT functions as biobehavioral synchronizer in parent-infant bonding and pair formation.

title: Probiotic microbes sustain youthful serum testosterone levels and testicular size in aging mice
finding: L. reuteri -> T up, testicular weight up, spermatogenesis up, Leydig cells up. Mechanism: IL-17 suppression.

title: Microbes and oxytocin: benefits for host physiology and behavior
finding: L. reuteri upregulates OT via vagus nerve. Immune-endocrine-brain signaling network.

title: Microbial symbionts accelerate wound healing via oxytocin
finding: L. reuteri accelerates wound healing through OT upregulation. Gut microbiome modulates systemic OT.

title: Wi-Fi exposure alters gut microbiome composition in mice
finding: Wi-Fi exposure changed Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio. EMF directly alters gut microbiome.

title: Membrane potential drives spermatogonial stem cell differentiation via mTOR
finding: Vmem depolarization -> mTOR activation -> premature SSC differentiation -> stem cell pool exhaustion.

title: Depolarization of sperm membrane potential in infertile men
finding: 10% of infertile men show fully depolarized Vmem. Direct link between bioelectric state and fertility.

title: Bioelectricity as a universal signaling mechanism
finding: Bioelectric signaling (Vmem patterns) is a universal mechanism controlling cell behavior, morphogenesis, and regeneration.

title: Temporal trends in sperm count: a systematic review and meta-regression analysis
finding: Sperm concentration declined 52.4% from 1973-2011 among Western men.

title: Temporal trends in sperm count: updated meta-regression
finding: Decline accelerated: -62% from 1973-2018. Global (not just Western). No sign of plateau.

title: Radiofrequency electromagnetic radiation and sperm quality
finding: RF-EMR from mobile phones reduces sperm motility, viability, and increases DNA fragmentation.

title: Is fertility reduced among men exposed to radiofrequency fields in the Norwegian Navy?
finding: OR 1.86 for infertility in RF-exposed Navy personnel. Dose-response. Sex ratio shift. N=10,497.

title: CatSper channel complex in human sperm fertilization
finding: CatSper is a 15+ subunit ion channel essential for capacitation, hyperactivation, chemotaxis, acrosome reaction. Voltage-gated.

title: Calcium channel blockers and male fertility
finding: CCBs (nifedipine, amlodipine) reduce sperm motility and acrosome reaction in clinical use. Confirms VGCC->fertility pathway.

title: Rapamycin (mTOR inhibitor) effects on fertility
finding: Rapamycin causes reversible male infertility in transplant patients. Confirms mTOR->spermatogenesis pathway.

title: The serotonin theory of depression: a systematic umbrella review
finding: No consistent evidence for serotonin deficiency in depression. SSRIs may work via other mechanisms. SSRIs cause sexual dysfunction -> fertility impact.

title: Metformin effects on biological aging in non-human primates
finding: Metformin reduced biological age by 6 years in primates. mTOR inhibition as anti-aging mechanism.

title: Non-thermal DNA breakage by mobile-phone radiation in human fibroblasts
finding: Intermittent exposure produced MORE DNA damage than continuous. Field transitions (off->on) critical. EU REFLEX consortium, 12 institutions.

title: Electromagnetic hypersensitivity: evidence for a novel neurological syndrome
finding: Double-blind provocation: symptoms from field transitions (off->on, on->off), not continuous field. 'EHS can occur as a bona fide neurological syndrome.'

title: Reactive oxygen species in Drosophila ovaries after EMF exposure
finding: Short EMF exposure: ROS recovered. Long exposure: ROS did NOT recover. Demonstrates repair capacity exhaustion.

title: EMF and mitochondrial ROS homeostasis
finding: Mitochondria especially vulnerable: ROS production feedback loop (damage -> more ROS -> more damage).

title: Electrohypersensitivity as a newly identified neurologic pathological disorder
finding: N~1000 EHS patients. Objective biomarkers: histaminemia up 40%, nitrotyrosine up 28%, S100B up 15%, melatonin down all cases. Consistent with VGCC/Ca2+/ROS/BBB pathway.

title: 5G RF-EMF effects on sleep EEG in CACNA1C genotyped volunteers
finding: First EMF study genotyping VGCC variants. 'Striking inter-individual differences in EMF response.' Sleep spindle modulation among most consistent EMF effects.

title: Wi-Fi exposure and HRV in healthy young volunteers
finding: Wi-Fi 2400 MHz: parasympathetic HF-HRV significantly reduced (p=0.036), sympathetic 0V% increased (p=0.002). Objective autonomic shift in healthy non-EHS volunteers.

title: More than 75 percent decline over 27 years in total flying insect biomass in protected areas
finding: 76% biomass decline 1989-2016 in 63 protected nature reserves. Weather explains variability but not trend.

title: Decline of the North American avifauna
finding: Net loss of 2.9 billion birds (-29%) since 1970. Largest declines in common species.

title: Canaries in the coal mine: a cross-species analysis of the plurality of obesity epidemics
finding: Laboratory and feral animals have also gotten fatter over 50 years despite controlled diets. Suggests environmental factor beyond diet/exercise.

title: The Body Electric: Electromagnetism and the Foundation of Life
finding: Pioneering work on bioelectricity. Documented EMF bioeffects and systematic suppression of research by military/industry.

title: Auditory system response to radio frequency energy
finding: Humans can 'hear' pulsed microwaves. First demonstration of non-thermal RF perception.

title: Tissue interactions with nonionizing electromagnetic fields
finding: Calcium efflux from brain tissue at specific EMF frequencies and amplitudes. Window effects.

authors: Lindgren J, Kovacs A, Liukkonen J
title: Geometric electrodynamics from Weyl geometry
finding: Derives electromagnetic field equations from Weyl geometry. Provides theoretical foundation for chi(A) selection rule.

title: Ambient conditions and semen quality across COVID periods
finding: Overall, semen quality improved during the COVID-19 pandemic. Sperm concentration increased post-COVID compared to pre-COVID era.

title: COVID temporarily impairs then recovers semen parameters
finding: Progressive motility and normal morphology significantly increased during recovery period. Sperm concentration rose during lockdown with 74-day spermatogenesis-cycle lag.

title: 6-month sperm recovery from COVID
finding: Sperm quality recovered 3-6 months post-infection. Repeated measurements confirm temporal pattern consistent with spermatogenesis cycle.

title: China COVID relaxation effect on semen quality
finding: When restrictions were LIFTED (December 2022), sperm quality DECLINED significantly (volume, concentration, motility all decreased). Reverse lockdown effect confirms BERM bidirectional prediction.

title: Connectivity and mobile trends survey (USA)
finding: 38% of population connected MORE devices during pandemic. Average US household: 25 connected devices. Permanent increase in indoor EMF environment.

title: UK screen-viewing pre vs post lockdown
finding: Total screen time 11-18% HIGHER post-lockdown than pre-COVID on weekdays. TV viewing 68% higher weekdays, 80% weekends. Change was PERMANENT.

title: US child screen time during COVID
finding: Children screen time increased by average 1.1 h/day. 3.4 devices disrupted parent-child interaction daily (previously 3.0).

title: India medical students screen time and sleep during COVID
finding: Median screen time rose from 5h to 8h/day during lockdown (p<0.001). Sleep disorder prevalence rose from 14.3% to 23.2% (p<0.05).

title: India household electricity consumption during COVID
finding: Household electricity consumption rose 15% overall, daytime 22-27.5%. Peak load shifted to morning (remote work). Direct proxy for indoor EMF increase.

title: Working from home adaptations and post-pandemic predictions
finding: Remote work share predicted to double: 18% pre to 37% post. 55% of US workers want hybrid. PERMANENT structural change in EMF exposure patterns.

title: Irreversible effects of COVID digitalization
finding: Irreversible effects — digitalization changes did not reverse after pandemic. Device counts, screen time and remote work remained permanently higher.

title: Netherlands child mental health 2018-2023 longitudinal
finding: Child mental health had NOT returned to pre-pandemic levels by April 2023. Previously observed trend towards pre-pandemic levels did not continue. Problems INCREASED further in psychiatric patients.

title: Switzerland natural experiment — screen time and mental health
journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
finding: Mental health problems increased over time with overall medium effect size (Hedge's g=0.337). Screen time increase associated with mental health decline in natural experiment design.

title: Screen time and child behavioral disorders during COVID (systematic review)
journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
finding: Indirect association between increased screen time and depression and anxiety. Systematic review 2019-2022.

title: One-year post-lockdown mental health trajectories
finding: Mental health problems did not recover 12 months after lockdown ended. Longitudinal study confirms persistence beyond social isolation period.

title: Evening device exposure and sleep during Italian lockdown
finding: Evening device exposure during lockdown altered sleep architecture. Effects accumulated over weeks of continuous exposure. Direct demonstration of recovery window elimination.

authors: Lea RG, Byers AS, Sumner RN, et al.
title: Environmental chemicals impact dog semen quality in vitro and may be associated with a temporal decline in sperm motility and increased cryptorchidism
finding: 26-year study (1988-2014) of stud dogs sharing human home environment. Progressive motility declined significantly. Normal morphology declined. Sperm concentration variable (rose then plateaued). Cryptorchidism prevalence changed. Environmental chemicals (DEHP, PCB153) detected in dog testes and commercial dog food at concentrations affecting sperm in vitro.

authors: Hensel B, Schmelz F, Gerstner K, et al.
title: Temporal trends in semen quality of breeding bulls and boars
finding: Bull (N=47,757, 1997-2019) and boar (N=619,368, 2005-2023) semen quality improved over study periods. Concentration and motility trends positive. Low-EMF production environments. However, improvement likely confounded by strong breeding selection pressure (sperm quality is direct selection criterion) and production environment advances.

title: The Body Electric: Electromagnetism and the Foundation of Life
finding: 17 clubfoot births in 16 months at Fort Rucker military hospital (expected: 4) in high-radar EMF environment. Investigation blocked by military classification of radiation maps.

authors: Guy AW, Chou CK, Lin JC, Christensen D
title: Chronic exposure of rats to 2.45 GHz microwaves (US Air Force SAM-TR-83-38)
finding: Rats exposed to 2.45 GHz at 0.5 mW/cm² for 25 months: 3.6× endocrine cancers (18 vs 5). Plasma cortisol pattern consistent with Selye GAS.

authors: Hydro-Québec survey (cited in Becker, Cross Currents)
title: Sex ratio shift in children of power station workers
journal: Cited in Becker RO, Cross Currents (1990)
finding: Sex ratio of offspring shifted from ~1:1 to 6:1 male after parental occupational EMF exposure at power generating stations.

authors: Zandieh A, Bhatt DK, Bhatt UC, Bhatt AN
title: Frequency-dependent effects of extremely low-frequency electromagnetic fields on mitochondrial membrane potential and reactive oxygen species
finding: Cells respond frequency-specifically to ELF fields in the 20-40 mHz range with distinct ROS and mitochondrial membrane potential (TMRM) patterns. Establishes the biological window (R42) that the 3GPP eDRX convergence targets.

title: Worldwide decline of the entomofauna: A review of its drivers
finding: 40% of insect species are declining globally, 33% are threatened with extinction. Rate of decline (~2.5% per year) implies catastrophic collapse within decades.

authors: Thielens A, Bell D, Mortimore DB, Greco MK, Martens L, Joseph W
title: Exposure of Insects to Radio-Frequency Electromagnetic Fields from 2 to 120 GHz
finding: Insects absorb 3-6 dB more power at 5G frequencies (6 GHz+) compared to current 4G bands due to body size resonance matching shorter wavelengths.

title: Anthropogenic radiofrequency electromagnetic fields as an emerging threat to wildlife orientation
finding: RF-EMF disrupts magnetoreception and orientation in insects, birds, and other wildlife. Proposes RF pollution as underrecognized driver of wildlife decline.

title: The incidence of electromagnetic pollution on the amphibian decline: Is this an important piece of the puzzle?
finding: Frog populations declined near mobile phone base stations. Tadpole mortality and developmental abnormalities correlated with RF exposure levels.

authors: Stuart SN, Chanson JS, Cox NA, Young BE, Rodrigues ASL, Fischman DL, Waller RW
title: Status and Trends of Amphibian Declines and Extinctions Worldwide
finding: Coined 'enigmatic decline' for amphibian population crashes with no identified cause. Nearly one-third of amphibian species are threatened globally.

title: Mobile phone-induced honeybee worker piping
finding: Active mobile phone handsets near hives triggered worker piping signals — a behavior normally associated with swarming or colony disturbance.

title: Changes in honeybee behaviour and biology under the influence of cellphone radiations
finding: RF-exposed colonies showed 50% reduced return rate of foraging bees. Queen egg-laying rate decreased and honey stores diminished.

authors: Shepherd S, Lima MAP, Oliveira EE, Sharkh SM, Jackson CW, Sherlock MR
title: Extremely low frequency electromagnetic fields impair the cognitive and motor abilities of honey bees
finding: ELF-EMF exposure at environmentally relevant levels reduced honeybee learning, flight, and foraging ability. Relevant to colony collapse disorder.

title: Threats to an ecosystem service: pressures on pollinators
journal: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
finding: Multi-factor analysis of pollinator decline. Identifies pesticides, habitat loss, disease, and environmental pollution as interacting stressors.

authors: Wang Y, Pan Y, Parsons S, Walker M, Zhang S
title: Bats respond to polarity of a magnetic field
journal: Proceedings of the Royal Society B
finding: Bats use magnetic polarity for orientation, demonstrating magnetoreception in mammals. Relevant to RF disruption of navigation systems.

authors: Frick WF, Pollock JF, Hicks AC, Langwig KE, Reynolds DS, Turner GG, Butchkoski CM, Kunz TH
title: An Emerging Disease Causes Regional Population Collapse of a Common North American Bat Species
finding: White-nose syndrome caused rapid bat population collapse. Demonstrates how environmental stressors can trigger sudden species decline in mammals.

title: Microwave effects on the blood-forming system with particular reference to the lymphocyte
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
finding: Chromosomal damage in sperm observed across a range of microwave exposures that span modern safety limits. Early evidence for non-thermal genetic effects.

authors: Panagopoulos DJ, Karabarbounis A, Margaritis LH
title: Effect of GSM 900-MHz Mobile Phone Radiation on the Reproductive Capacity of Drosophila melanogaster
finding: GSM 900 MHz exposure decreased Drosophila reproductive capacity by up to 60%. Effect was dose-dependent and partially reversible after cessation.

authors: Gandhi OP, Lazzi G, Furse CM
title: Electromagnetic absorption in the human head and neck for mobile telephones at 835 and 1900 MHz
journal: IEEE Transactions on Microwave Theory and Techniques
finding: SAR distribution in the head varies with skull geometry. Children absorb 2-3× the SAR of adults due to thinner skulls and higher tissue conductivity.

title: Has East Germany Overtaken West Germany? Recent Trends in Order-Specific Fertility
finding: East German TFR collapsed from 1.5 to 0.77 after reunification (1990-1994), then recovered. Demonstrates fertility can undergo rapid environmental-shock collapse and partial recovery.

authors: Belpomme D, Campagnac C, Irigaray P
title: Reliable disease biomarkers characterizing and identifying electrohypersensitivity and multiple chemical sensitivity as two etiopathogenic aspects of a unique pathological disorder
finding: Identified blood biomarkers (histamine, S100B, nitrotyrosine, heat shock proteins) in EHS patients. Suggests objective biological basis for electromagnetic hypersensitivity.

authors: Huss A, Egger M, Hug K, Huwiler-Müntener K, Röösli M
title: Source of Funding and Results of Studies of Health Effects of Mobile Phone Use: Systematic Review of Experimental Studies
finding: Industry-funded studies were substantially less likely to report statistically significant effects than independently funded studies. Funding source is a significant predictor of study outcome.

title: Eurobarometer: Fertility and family issues
finding: Europeans desire 2.3 children on average but achieve only 1.5. The fertility gap has widened over time, suggesting structural barriers beyond individual choice.

authors: Vassallo G, Catania F, Ferro M
title: Independent validation of Lindgren geometric electrodynamics derivation
finding: Independently validated the Lindgren derivation of electromagnetic field equations from Weyl geometry, confirming the mathematical foundation of the chi(A) selection rule.

title: Toxicology and carcinogenesis studies in Hsd:Sprague Dawley SD rats exposed to whole-body radio frequency radiation at a frequency (900 MHz)
finding: Clear evidence of heart schwannomas and some evidence of brain gliomas in male rats exposed to 2G/3G cell phone radiation. Largest animal RF study ever conducted ($30M, 10 years).

authors: Falcioni L, Bua L, Tibaldi E, Lauriola M, De Angelis L, Thayer GP, Gnudi G, Mandrioli D, Manservigi M, Manservisi F, Manzoli I, Menghetti I, Montella R, Panzacchi S, Sgargi D, Strollo V, Vornoli A, Belpoggi F
title: Report of final results regarding brain and heart tumors in Sprague-Dawley rats exposed from prenatal life until natural death to mobile phone radiofrequency field
finding: Ramazzini Institute replication of NTP findings at lower, environmentally relevant RF levels. Found same tumor types (schwannomas, glial tumors) at far-field exposure levels.

authors: IARC Working Group on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans
title: Non-ionizing radiation, Part 2: Radiofrequency electromagnetic fields
journal: IARC Monographs on the Evaluation of Carcinogenic Risks to Humans, Vol. 102
finding: WHO/IARC classified RF electromagnetic fields as Group 2B (possibly carcinogenic to humans) based on limited evidence from epidemiological studies of glioma and acoustic neuroma.

title: Brain tumour risk in relation to mobile telephone use: results of the INTERPHONE international case-control study
finding: Largest international case-control study of mobile phone use and brain tumors (13 countries). Heaviest users showed elevated glioma risk (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.03-1.89).

authors: Agarwal A, Desai NR, Makker K, Varghese A, Mouradi R, Sabanegh E, Sharma R
title: Effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic waves (RF-EMW) from cellular phones on human ejaculated semen: an in vitro pilot study
finding: RF-EMW exposure from cell phones decreased sperm motility and viability, and increased ROS production in human semen samples in vitro.

authors: Adams JA, Galloway TS, Mondal D, Esteves SC, Mathews F
title: Effect of mobile telephones on sperm quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis
finding: Meta-analysis of 10 studies: mobile phone exposure associated with reduced sperm motility (8.1% mean difference) and viability (9.1%). Effects consistent across in vitro and in vivo studies.

authors: De Iuliis GN, Newey RJ, King BV, Aitken RJ
title: Mobile phone radiation induces reactive oxygen species production and DNA damage in human spermatozoa in vitro
finding: 1800 MHz RF exposure induced dose-dependent ROS production and DNA fragmentation in human spermatozoa. Effect mediated through mitochondrial ROS generation.

authors: Avendaño C, Mata A, Sanchez Sarmiento CA, Doncel GF
title: Use of laptop computers connected to internet through Wi-Fi decreases human sperm motility and increases sperm DNA fragmentation
finding: 4-hour WiFi laptop exposure decreased sperm motility by 25% and increased DNA fragmentation vs. controls. Effect beyond thermal contribution.

authors: Kesari KK, Agarwal A, Henkel R
title: Radiations and male fertility
finding: Comprehensive review: RF-EMR affects sperm count, motility, viability, and morphology through oxidative stress, DNA damage, and apoptosis pathways.

authors: La Vignera S, Condorelli RA, Vicari E, D'Agata R, Calogero AE
title: Effects of the exposure to mobile phones on male reproduction: a review of the literature
finding: Review of human and animal studies: mobile phone exposure consistently associated with decreased sperm concentration, motility, normal morphology, and viability.

authors: Skakkebaek NE, Rajpert-De Meyts E, Buck Louis GM, Toppari J, Andersson AM, Eisenberg ML, Jensen TK, Jorgensen N, Swan SH, Sapra KJ, Ziebe S, Priskorn L, Juul A
title: Male Reproductive Disorders and Fertility Trends: Influences of Environment and Genetic Susceptibility
finding: Comprehensive review of male reproductive health trends: declining sperm counts, increasing testicular cancer, cryptorchidism, and hypospadias. Environmental factors implicated as primary drivers.

authors: Carlsen E, Giwercman A, Keiding N, Skakkebaek NE
title: Evidence for decreasing quality of semen during past 50 years
finding: Meta-analysis of 61 studies (1938-1991): mean sperm count declined from 113 to 66 million/mL. First systematic evidence of global semen quality decline.

authors: Swan SH, Elkin EP, Fenster L
title: The question of declining sperm density revisited: an analysis of 101 studies published 1934-1996
finding: Confirmed Carlsen 1992 findings with expanded dataset: sperm density decline of ~1.5% per year in US and Europe. Decline accelerating in later decades.

title: Electromagnetic fields stress living cells
finding: EMF activates cellular stress response (HSP70, HSP27) at non-thermal levels. DNA acts as a fractal antenna for EMF interaction, with response thresholds far below thermal.

authors: Friedman J, Kraus S, Hauptman Y, Schiff Y, Seger R
title: Mechanism of short-term ERK activation by electromagnetic fields at mobile phone frequencies
finding: 875 MHz RF activated ERK cascade via NADH oxidase → ROS → matrix metalloproteinases. Established a complete non-thermal signaling pathway from RF exposure to gene transcription.

authors: Panagopoulos DJ, Johansson O, Carlo GL
title: Polarization: A Key Difference between Man-made and Natural Electromagnetic Fields, in regard to Biological Activity
finding: Man-made (polarized) EMFs are far more biologically active than natural (unpolarized) fields at the same intensity. Polarization enables coherent forcing of charged molecules.

title: Magnetic-field-induced DNA strand breaks in brain cells of the rat
finding: ELF magnetic fields (60 Hz) induced both single- and double-strand DNA breaks in rat brain cells at non-thermal levels. Effect blocked by free radical scavengers.

authors: Volkow ND, Tomasi D, Wang GJ, Vaska P, Fowler JS, Telang F, Alexoff D, Logan J, Wong C
title: Effects of Cell Phone Radiofrequency Signal Exposure on Brain Glucose Metabolism
finding: 50-minute cell phone exposure increased brain glucose metabolism in the region closest to the antenna (7% increase, p<0.001). Demonstrates RF biological activity in human brain.

title: Microwave frequency electromagnetic fields (EMFs) produce widespread neuropsychiatric effects including depression
finding: VGCC activation by microwave EMFs in the brain produces neuropsychiatric effects: sleep disturbance, headache, cognitive dysfunction, depression, fatigue, and anxiety.

authors: Cucurachi S, Tamis WLM, Vijver MG, Peijnenburg WJGM, Bolte JFB, de Snoo GR
title: A review of the ecological effects of radiofrequency electromagnetic fields (RF-EMF)
finding: Review of 113 studies: 65% reported significant ecological effects of RF-EMF on birds, insects, other vertebrates, other organisms, and plants.

title: Electromagnetic pollution from phone masts. Effects on wildlife
finding: Review of wildlife effects near cell towers: altered bird nesting behavior, reduced reproductive success in storks, behavioral changes in multiple species.

authors: Belyaev I, Dean A, Eger H, Hubmann G, Jandrisovits R, Kern M, Kundi M, Moshammer H, Lercher P, Müller K, Oberfeld G, Ohnsorge P, Pelzmann P, Scheingraber C, Thill R
title: EUROPAEM EMF Guideline 2016 for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of EMF-related health problems and illnesses
finding: European Academy for Environmental Medicine guidelines: current ICNIRP limits are inadequate for non-thermal effects. Recommends precautionary reference levels 100-1000× lower.

title: Mobile phone and cordless phone use and the risk for glioma — analysis of pooled case-control studies in Sweden, 1997-2003 and 2007-2009
finding: Pooled Swedish case-control studies: long-term mobile phone use (>25 years) associated with increased glioma risk (OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.7-5.2). Risk highest for ipsilateral exposure.

authors: Miller AB, Sears ME, Morgan LL, Davis DL, Hardell L, Oremus M, Soskolne CL
title: Risks to Health and Well-Being From Radio-Frequency Radiation Emitted by Cell Phones and Other Wireless Devices
finding: Cancer epidemiology update: evidence since IARC 2011 classification strengthens case for upgrading RF-EMF from Group 2B to Group 1 (carcinogenic to humans).

title: Commentary on the utility of the National Toxicology Program study on cell phone radiofrequency radiation data for assessing human health risks despite unfounded criticisms
finding: Senior NTP scientist defends study design and findings against industry criticism. Argues NTP results provide clear evidence of carcinogenicity and should inform safety standards.

title: Stress and the General Adaptation Syndrome
finding: Defined the three-stage General Adaptation Syndrome: alarm, resistance, exhaustion. Foundation for understanding chronic low-level stressor effects on biological systems.

title: The absorption of electromagnetic energy in body tissues
finding: Established 10 mW/cm² thermal threshold that became the basis for US safety standards. Defined the thermal-only paradigm that persists in ICNIRP guidelines.
